findings.claim: Baselining the check `http-header-validation:sep-2243-server-accepts-whitespace-header-value` masks that check by ID, not by failure cause, so a future genuine header-validation regression (the behavior the check actually exists to verify) would be silently accepted by CI.
findings.evidence: The baseline entry is justified in the YAML comment and verification.md as 'the runner invokes the first listed tool with `{}`; Compass ... correctly requires `query`' — i.e., the observed failure cause is unrelated to whitespace header validation. verification.md asserts 'The one baselined header-runner check is the invalid-argument invocation described above, not a header mismatch failure,' but nothing in a check-granular expected-failure mechanism can enforce that distinction; any failure of that check ID, including the header-acceptance defect it names, matches the baseline. design.md simultaneously claims 'transport, wire-schema, routing, or advertised capability failure remains a blocking failure.'
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove this entry and make the first listed tool tolerant of `{}` invocation for the header scenario, or verify the runner supports cause/strict matching (fail on unexpected pass or mismatched failure reason) and document that enforcement; otherwise record the header-validation coverage gap explicitly in the spec/verification artifacts.

findings.claim: The committed PROGRESS LEDGER lists C-010 as '[PENDING]' in the same diff that adds C-010 completion evidence (tasks 1.1–3.1 checked, refiner receipt 'Status: PASS'), leaving repository-owned KBD certification evidence internally contradictory.
findings.evidence: execution.md PROGRESS LEDGER: '- [PENDING] C-010 — SELF/OpenSpec, gated by C-008 and C-009' (also '[IN_PROGRESS] C-001'), while openspec/changes/mcp-conformance-interop/tasks.md shows '- [x] 2.1' and '- [x] 3.1', and .refiner/artifacts/C-010/dist/refinement-receipt.md states 'Status: **PASS**'. The constraint `refiner-qa-evidence` requires these tracked artifacts to be deterministic and consistent certification evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the execution.md ledger (or annotate it as an execution-start snapshot with a pointer to progress.json as the live projection) before archiving C-010.

findings.claim: The reproduction section tells the reader to 'reproduce the held Codex HTTP cell,' but the recorded matrix shows the Codex CLI 0.150.1 HTTP cell as PASS — no Codex cell is held.
findings.evidence: The same document's matrix: '| Codex CLI | `0.150.1` | PASS — `Nodes: 120215` | PASS — `Nodes: 120215` |' and the text 'Codex 0.146.0 initially failed the HTTP cell, but the isolated official 0.150.1 release passed both cells'; the only incompatible cell is OpenCode 1.18.25 HTTP.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the final line to reference reproducing the recorded Codex HTTP pass (or the OpenCode HTTP incompatibility, if that was the intent).

findings.claim: The final success message 'MCP conformance passed: stdio=native HTTP=reference@...' is printed by a script that exercises only HTTP, implying a stdio result it did not produce — misleading when the script is run standalone as the docs' reproduction section instructs.
findings.evidence: The script's loop runs only `--scenario server-stateless/tools-list/...` against `--url http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/mcp`; stdio coverage is the separate `cargo test -p compass-mcp --test protocol_conformance` CI leg. docs/implementation/mcp-conformance-and-interop.md lists `scripts/qualify_mcp_conformance.sh` alone as a reproduction command.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the echo to report only the HTTP leg (e.g., 'MCP HTTP conformance passed: reference@<ref> spec=2026-07-28; stdio leg = cargo test -p compass-mcp --test protocol_conformance').
